turns.question: Where is middleware composition implemented?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the hono repository structure using gh CLI without cloning.`src/compose.ts` looks like the key file. Let me examine it and its usage in `hono-base.ts`.Now let's see how `compose` is invoked from the router/dispatch layer in `hono-base.ts`.I now have concrete evidence. Let me also quickly check the router's `match` return shape to confirm what array `compose` receives, for completeness.I have enough to give a complete, well-evidenced answer.

## Where middleware composition is implemented

**Core composition algorithm: `src/compose.ts`, function `compose`** (lines 15–68)

This is the actual engine — a koa-compose-style continuation chain (the file's own docstring says "based on `koa-compose` package"):
- `compose(middleware, onError?, onNotFound?)` returns `(context, next) => Promise<Context>`.
- Internally it defines `dispatch(i)` (line 32), a recursive async function that:
  - guards against calling `next()` more than once (`if (i <= index) throw new Error('next() called multiple times')`)
  - pulls the i-th handler out of the middleware array: `handler = middleware[i][0][0]` (line 43)
  - invokes it as `await handler(context, () => dispatch(i + 1))` (line 51) — this is what makes `next()` inside a middleware advance the chain
  - wraps the call in try/catch, routing thrown `Error`s to the supplied `onError` handler (lines 53–56)
  - if no handler exists for index `i` and the context isn't finalized, calls `onNotFound` (lines 62–63)
- The returned value of each call becomes `context.res` when appropriate, and the whole chain resolves to the final `Context`.

**Where `compose` is invoked / middleware array is assembled: `src/hono-base.ts`**

- `this.use = (...)` (line 157) is how `app.use(...)` registers middleware — it stores them as routes via `#addRoute` (line 165), tagged with method `ALL` (`METHOD_NAME_ALL`) and a path, exactly like regular route handlers. So in Hono, middleware and route handlers are unified into the same router entries.
- `#addRoute` (line 385) calls `this.router.add(method, path, [handler, r])` (line 395), storing each handler alongside its `RouterRoute` metadata in the router (see `src/router.ts`, `Router<T>.add`/`match` interface, and the actual trie/regex implementations under `src/router/`).
- `#dispatch` (line 406) is the real per-request entry point:
  - looks up `matchResult = this.router.match(method, path)` (line 411) — this returns all matched handlers for that path, in order (middleware first, then the route handler), per `Result<T>` in `src/router.ts`.
  - **Fast path optimization** (line 430): `if (matchResult[0].length === 1)` — if there's exactly one matched handler (no middleware), it's called directly without going through `compose` at all.
  - **General path** (line 450): `const composed = compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)` — this is the actual call site that turns the matched array of `[handler, route]` tuples into the single composed function, which is then invoked with the `Context`.

**Route-grouping edge case: also in `hono-base.ts`, `.route()` (~line 224–229)**
When sub-apps have a custom `errorHandler`, `compose([], app.errorHandler)` is used to wrap a single sub-route handler so its error handler still applies when mounted into a parent app.

### Evidence
All of the above was read directly from the `main` branch via `gh api repos/honojs/hono/contents/<path>` (base64-decoded), with line numbers confirmed via `grep -n` on the decoded source — not guessed from memory or docs.

### What I did not verify
- I did not inspect the concrete router implementations (`src/router/reg-exp-router`, `src/router/trie-router`, `src/router/smart-router`, `src/router/linear-router`, `src/router/pattern-router`) to confirm exactly how `matchResult[0]` orders middleware vs. handlers for nested `.route()`/`.basePath()` cases — I only confirmed the `Router<T>` interface shape in `src/router.ts`.
- I did not check `src/compose.test.ts` / `src/hono.test.ts` for behavioral edge cases (e.g., multiple `onError` layers, RPC client composition).
- I did not check whether any adapter-specific code (e.g., `src/adapter/*`) does additional composition — this appears to live solely in framework-core (`compose.ts` + `hono-base.ts`).
